cases.explain: Молчание is the subject of the intransitive verb наступает (falls/sets in), so it takes the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Хромая люстра, взятая на прокат из ___.
cases.translation: The crooked chandelier, rented from the tavern.
cases.explain: The preposition из (from/out of) always governs the genitive case: трактира.

cases.sentence: А по моему ___ электрическое освещение — одно только жульничество!
cases.translation: But in my view, electric lighting is nothing but a swindle!
cases.explain: The preposition по (according to) here governs the dative case: взгляду.

cases.sentence: Ежели бы вы видели электрическую ___, из чего она составлена.
cases.translation: If you had seen the electric battery, what it's made of.
cases.explain: Видеть (to see) is transitive; its direct object takes the accusative case: батарею.

cases.translation: Those at supper listen to him with some disdain.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) expressing manner governs the instrumental case: пренебрежением.

cases.translation: In the widow Mymrina's house there is a wedding supper.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) marking location takes the prepositional case: доме.

reading.ru: В доме вдовы мымрены, что в пятисобачьем переулке свадебный ужин.
reading.question: Where does the wedding supper take place?
options: In the house of the widow Mymrina, on Five-Dog Lane
In a rented banquet hall downtown
In a restaurant near the station
reading.correct: In the house of the widow Mymrina, on Five-Dog Lane
reading.explain: The story opens with the wedding supper taking place in the widow Mymrina's house on Five-Dog Lane.

reading.ru: Ужинает двадцать три человека, из коих восемь ничего не едят.
reading.question: How many guests are having supper, and how many of them aren't eating anything?
options: Twenty-three guests, eight of whom eat nothing
Ten guests, none of whom eat
Thirty guests, all of whom eat heartily
reading.correct: Twenty-three guests, eight of whom eat nothing
reading.explain: The narrator notes twenty-three people are at supper, and eight of them eat nothing, complaining of feeling sick.

reading.ru: А по моему взгляду электрическое освещение — одно только жульничество!
reading.question: What is the best man's opinion of electric lighting?
options: That it is nothing but a swindle
That it is the future of Russia
That it is too expensive for ordinary people
That it is dangerous and should be banned
reading.correct: That it is nothing but a swindle
reading.explain: The best man grumbles that in his view, electric lighting is nothing but a swindle.

reading.ru: - Ежели бы вы видели электрическую батарею, из чего она составлена, говорит телеграфист, рисуясь, - то вы иначе бы рассуждали.
reading.question: What does the telegraph operator suggest would change people's minds about electricity?
options: Seeing what an electric battery is made of
reading.correct: Seeing what an electric battery is made of
reading.explain: The telegraph operator argues that if they had seen what an electric battery is composed of, they would think differently.

reading.question: How does the best man respond to the idea of learning more about electricity?
options: He says he has no desire to see such swindling
He asks to see the battery immediately
He agrees to change his opinion
He laughs and changes the subject
reading.correct: He says he has no desire to see such swindling
reading.explain: The best man retorts that he has no wish to see such trickery, insisting simple folk are being cheated.

reading.ru: - Я с вами, папаша, вполне согласен, - говорит хриплым тенором жених Апломбов, молодой человек с длинной шеей и щетинистыми волосами.
reading.question: How does the groom Aplombov initially respond to the argument about electricity?
options: He agrees fully with the best man
He sides with the telegraph operator
He asks for the argument to continue
reading.correct: He agrees fully with the best man
reading.explain: The groom, speaking in a hoarse tenor, says he is in full agreement with his father-in-law and would rather everyone just drink.

reading.ru: Они хочут свою образованность показать и всегда говорят о непонятном.
reading.question: How does the bride Dashenka react when asked her opinion about the argument?
options: She complains that people just want to show off their education by talking about incomprehensible things
She agrees enthusiastically with the telegraph operator
She changes the subject to the wedding cake
reading.correct: She complains that people just want to show off their education by talking about incomprehensible things
reading.explain: Dashenka blushes and says such people just want to show off their learning by talking about things no one understands.

reading.ru: - Слава богу, прожили век без образования и вот уж, благодарить бога, третью дочку за хорошего человека выдаем, - говорит с другого конца стола мать Дашеньки, вздыхая и обращаясь к телеграфисту.
reading.question: What does Dashenka's mother say about their family's lack of formal education?
options: That they lived their whole lives without education, thank God
That she regrets not sending Dashenka to school
That the groom insisted on educating Dashenka
reading.correct: That they lived their whole lives without education, thank God
reading.explain: Dashenka's mother says thank God they lived their whole life without education, and are now marrying off their third daughter to a good man.

reading.question: How does the groom Aplombov react to the telegraph operator's remark about marrying for money?
options: He accuses him of making an insinuation, growing red in the face
He asks the operator to leave immediately
reading.correct: He accuses him of making an insinuation, growing red in the face
reading.explain: Aplombov, turning red and blinking, exclaims that this is an insinuation, taking offense.

reading.ru: Кроме того, что мы тысячу рублей, мы три соло подаем, постелю и вот эту всю мебель.
reading.question: What does Dashenka's mother list as part of the dowry?
options: A thousand rubles, three place settings/sets, bedding, and all the furniture
A house in the countryside and a carriage
Jewelry and a dowry of gold coins
reading.correct: A thousand rubles, three place settings/sets, bedding, and all the furniture
reading.explain: The mother insists the dowry is not trifling, listing a thousand rubles, three sets, bedding, and all the furniture.

reading.question: What does Aplombov shout at the telegraph operator during the argument?
options: That he should pay for the supper
That he should marry Dashenka instead
reading.explain: Enraged, Aplombov repeatedly shouts at the telegraph operator that he should get out of the house.

reading.ru: Только вы отдайте мне сначала три рубля, что вы у меня на пикейную жилетку заняли.
reading.question: What does the telegraph operator demand before he agrees to leave?
options: That the groom first return three rubles he borrowed for a waistcoat
That he be given another glass of wine
That the bride apologize to him
That he be paid for his telegraph services
reading.correct: That the groom first return three rubles he borrowed for a waistcoat
reading.explain: The flustered telegraph operator says he'll leave but insists Aplombov first repay the three rubles borrowed for a pique waistcoat.

reading.ru: В воздухе от земли до крыш кружится что-то белое, очень похожее на снег.
reading.question: What strange white substance do the neighbors notice filling the air the next morning?
options: Something white, very much like snow
reading.correct: Something white, very much like snow
reading.explain: The next morning something white, resembling snow, is seen swirling in the air from the ground up to the rooftops.

reading.question: What crime does the passing dvornik (yardman) report has occurred?
reading.explain: The yardman tells the laundresses that the groom was robbed, giving them the news of the morning's commotion.

reading.ru: Перины жалко, отвечает за нее мать.
reading.question: What does Dashenka's mother lament as the procession passes by?
options: The loss of the feather mattress and its down
The cost of the wedding supper
reading.correct: The loss of the feather mattress and its down
reading.explain: As Dashenka cries, her mother answers for her, lamenting the loss of the feather mattress — three poods of down, every feather perfect.

highlight.question: Which sentence indicates how the guests responded to the telegraph operator's remarks about electricity?
sentences: В доме вдовы Мымриной, что в Пятисобачьем переулке, свадебный ужин.
Ужинает 23 человека, из коих восемь ничего не едят, клюют носом и жалуются, что их "мутит".

Свечи, лампы и хромая люстра, взятая напрокат из трактира, горят до того ярко, что один из гостей, сидящих за столом, телеграфист, кокетливо щурит глаза и то и дело заговаривает об электрическом освещении ни к селу ни к городу.
Этому освещению и вообще электричеству он пророчит блестящую будущность, но, тем не менее, ужинающие слушают его с некоторым пренебрежением.
highlight.explain: This sentence reveals that despite the operator's predictions about electric lighting's bright future, the diners listened to him with disdain and contempt.

highlight.question: Which two sentences show Aplombov agreeing with the telegraph operator while objecting to the timing of such discussions?
sentences: - Я с вами, папаша, вполне согласен, - говорит хриплым тенором жених Апломбов, молодой человек с длинной шеей и щетинистыми волосами.
- К чему заводить ученые разговоры?
Я не прочь и сам поговорить о всевозможных открытиях в научном смысле, но ведь на это есть другое время!
Ты какого мнения, машер?  (11) - обращается жених к сидящей рядом невесте.
highlight.explain: The first shows his agreement, and the second expresses his view that scientific discussions are appropriate at other times, not during a wedding dinner.

highlight.question: Which two sentences demonstrate the speaker's respect for the bride's family and his concern about marriages motivated by financial gain?
sentences: - Я, Татьяна Петровна, всегда уважал ваше семейство, - говорит он, - а ежели я насчет электрического освещения, так это еще не значит, что я из гордости.
Даже вот выпить могу...
Я всегда от всех чувств желал Дарье Ивановне хорошего жениха.
В наше время, Татьяна Петровна, трудно выйти за хорошего человека.
Нынче каждый норовит вступить в брак из-за интереса, из-за денег...
highlight.explain: The first shows his respect for the family, and the last reveals his worry that in modern times men marry for money rather than genuine affection.

highlight.question: Which two sentences capture the mother's reproach that she was not warned earlier and her direct accusation of the groom?
sentences: - А вы не намекайте, - говорит невестина мать.
- Мы вас по вашим родителям почитаем и на свадьбу пригласили, а вы разные слова...
А ежели вы знали, что Егор Федорыч из интереса женится, то что же вы раньше молчали?
Пришли бы да и сказали по-родственному: так и так, мол, на интерес польстился...
А тебе, батюшка, грех!
- обращается вдруг невестина мать к жениху, слезливо мигая глазами.
- Я ее, может, вскормила, вспоила...  берегла пуще алмаза изумрудного, деточку мою, а ты...  ты из интереса...
highlight.explain: The first asks why the telegraph operator did not warn her if he knew about the groom's mercenary motives, and the second is her emotional accusation directed at the groom.

highlight.question: Which two sentences show the telegraph operator being bewildered by the situation and insisting on repayment of his debt?
sentences: - Я ничего...
- говорит ошеломленный телеграфист, поднимаясь из-за стола.
- Не понимаю даже...
Извольте, я уйду...
Только вы отдайте мне сначала три рубля, что вы у меня на пикейную жилетку заняли.
Выпью вот еще и...  уйду, только вы сначала долг отдайте.
highlight.explain: The first shows his confusion and denial of involvement, and the second reveals his practical concern about recovering the three rubles borrowed for his vest.

highlight.question: Which two sentences show the growing confusion among the guests about what has transpired?
sentences: Те в ответ машут руками и бегут дальше...
Они и сами не знают, в чем дело.
Но вот, наконец, медленно проходит один дворник и, беседуя сам с собой, жестикулирует руками.
Очевидно, он побывал на месте происшествия и знает всё.
highlight.explain: These sentences indicate that the guests themselves are confused about what the matter is, though the janitor's arrival suggests he has information about the cause of the disturbance.
